subject: sociology
title: Inequality in the Classroom
welcome_lead: Why do different groups get different results? Apply class, gender and ethnicity studies to GCSE achievement.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying Bowles & Gintis and achievement gap studies to education.
final_note: Always link a gap (class, gender, ethnicity) to a study and an explanation.

concepts.def: Bowles & Gintis: school mirrors workplace hierarchy.
Bourdieu: middle-class knowledge that helps in school.
Lacking money for books, tuition or quiet study space.
Teachers giving pupils a fixed identity, e.g. 'bright'.
Pupils live up — or down — to their label.
Treating schools like a market with parental choice.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bowles and Gintis (1976) argue education is not meritocratic. The correspondence principle means school life (bells, obedience, rewards) mirrors factory life, training working-class pupils for low-paid jobs.

walkthroughs.h2: Why do poorer pupils score lower?
walkthroughs.body_html: Material deprivation (no quiet bedroom, no laptop), cultural deprivation (less help with homework) and schools labelling working-class pupils as less able combine to widen the gap.
The 1988 Act introduced league tables, Ofsted and parental choice. Critics say middle-class parents 'game' the system, while struggling schools fall further behind.

mcqs.q: Bowles & Gintis are linked to which idea?
Cultural capital is associated with which thinker?

numericals.q: In what year was the Education Reform Act that introduced league tables and Ofsted passed?

free_texts.q: What two-word term names a pupil living up to a teacher's expectation?
